text:
Sara (Sales): Hey team — ACME procurement says they'll sign an NDA but the signer name they provided doesn't match the account name we have on file. They insist on an exact corporate match (they want 'Acme Holdings, Inc.' but their buyer signed as 'Acme LLC'). They're saying SOC 2 report is required to move the POC. Can we unblock quickly? @Maya (Security) @Tom (Legal)

Kevin (Solutions Eng): Quick question — would a redacted SOC 2 extract (system description + control matrix) + a signed attestation letter be sufficient for their risk team? Alternatively, can we provide a time-limited read-only view if legal signs off?

Maya (Security): We have three practical paths: 1) Full: they provide an authorized signer name that matches and we deliver full SOC 2 under standard NDA. 2) Interim: we publish a redacted "SOC2 summary pack" + Head of Security attestation (no raw evidence). 3) Live review: a 30–45min walkthrough with our security SME to demonstrate controls and evidence live (screen-share, no file transfer). Options 2/3 are okay for preliminary risk validation but Legal needs to confirm nondisclosure wording. We also log access and watermark.

Tom (Legal): We can't accept a signature mismatch on the NDA unless procurement provides formal authorization (corporate resolution or an authorization email on letterhead). We can consider a limited "bridge-letter"/attestation but Counsel must approve final wording. If they want the full report, the executed NDA must name the actual legal entity that will receive the report. Jenna, can you ask them for a signing authority doc?

Jenna (Acct Exec): I'll ping the buyer now for an authorization scan or a PO showing the legal entity. If they can't produce that immediately, can we offer the redacted viewer for 72 hours as an interim? Maya, would that satisfy the customer's security team for now?

Maya (Security): Yes — a secure viewer (no-download, dynamic watermark, 72h expiry) + an attestation letter should be acceptable as a short-term fix. We will also include a 1-page controls summary and the system description. Legal needs to confirm the viewer's access terms match NDA obligations; we need an audit trail of access.

Sara (Sales): Plan: Jenna to collect the authorization doc by EOD tomorrow. If we get it, Legal/Tom will fast-track NDA signature. If not, we'll provide the secure viewer + attestation letter and schedule a live walkthrough with Kevin for technical Qs. Tentative walkthrough slot: Thu 10am PT — Maya/Kevin available. @docu-sign-bot queue our standard NDA template for acme@acme.com but hold final send until Jenna confirms the exact legal entity.

docu-sign-bot: Queued "Standard Vendor NDA v3". Note: signature party name must match executed entity. Use the "exception" field to record any temporary deviations.

Tom (Legal): I'll draft a short bridge-letter template and circulate before 6pm today. If buyer provides a scanned board resolution or signed authorization, we can skip the bridge-letter.

Kevin (Solutions Eng): If they ask about data residency or network controls in the walkthrough, I can present the infra diagram + isolation slide deck and answer network/VPC questions. I'll prepare a short tech pack for the session.

Jenna (Acct Exec): Update — ACME replied: they can provide a Corporate Signing Authority PDF within 24 hours. I'm asking them to send it to acme-legal@redwood.com. I'll update thread when I get it.

Sara (Sales): Thanks team, sounds good. I'll hold the POC kickoff until we have either the signed NDA with matching entity or the secure-viewer + attestation in place. :thumbsup:
